# Reset-PrintSpooler

Clears stuck print jobs by stopping the Print Spooler, emptying the spool folder and starting it again.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | Yes |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Yes |
| **Admin rights** | Yes (except with `-WhatIf`) |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Reset-PrintSpooler.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Reset-PrintSpooler.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Reset-PrintSpooler.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

The standard fix when documents are stuck in the print queue and cannot be cancelled (see KB-012):

1. Stop the Print Spooler service
2. Delete the spool files (*.SHD / *.SPL) in the spool folder
3. Start the Print Spooler service and confirm it is running

All pending print jobs on this computer are deleted, so tell the user to print again afterwards. Supports -WhatIf and -Confirm. Requires an elevated (administrator) session, except with -WhatIf.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-SpoolPath` | String | `(Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'System32\spool\PRINTERS')` | Folder with the spool files. Default: %SystemRoot%\System32\spool\PRINTERS. |
| `-ServiceName` | String | `'Spooler'` | Name of the spooler service. Default: Spooler. |
| `-TimeoutSeconds` | Int32 | `30` | How long to wait for the service to stop or start. Default 30. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Reset-PrintSpooler.ps1 -WhatIf
```

Shows what would be done and how many jobs would be deleted.

```powershell
.\Reset-PrintSpooler.ps1 -Confirm:$false
```

From an elevated prompt, resets the spooler without prompting.

## Notes

Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. Related KB: KB-012 Printer Shows Offline or Jobs Are Stuck in the Queue.
